Who we are

A home for prevention-focused action on AMR.

The Prevention of Infection Committee is a Geneva Health Forum initiative bringing together international expertise from science, clinical practice, public health, policy and civil society.

The PIC Plenary sets priorities and makes decisions. Under the Geneva Health Forum, the Scientific Coordination Team provides neutral scientific and administrative support—developing concept notes, synthesizing evidence and preparing proposals for committee review.

How it started. PIC grew from the November 2025 symposium on infection prevention and AMR, where participants called for a long-term, action-oriented structure able to translate priorities into measurable projects.

Direction

Prevention first—then evidence, partnership and implementation.

Our vision

A world in which infection prevention is recognized, adequately funded and systematically implemented as the primary strategy to control antimicrobial resistance, across all settings, populations and health systems.

Our mission

Bring expertise together to turn scientific and policy insights into actionable recommendations and feasible implementation initiatives.

What we do

We move promising prevention priorities towards action.

PIC is designed as a pragmatic, multi-year programme—not simply an advisory group. Its work connects evidence, committee expertise and implementation opportunities.

Synthesize evidence

Review scientific literature, guidance and implementation experience to clarify what is known and where gaps remain.

Develop concepts

Translate priority problems into structured concept notes and decision-ready proposals for PIC review.

Enable implementation

Connect selected priorities with technical partners, pilot settings, evaluation approaches and routes to scale.

Funding & scientific independence

OM Pharma provides an educational grant to GHF to support scientific coordination. PIC members participate pro bono, and scientific priorities and decisions remain under PIC governance.

Structure & responsibilities

Governance

The PIC Plenary is the highest governing body. The Scientific Coordination Team supports the committee’s work, within GHF’s institutional environment.

PIC Plenary

Sets strategic direction, reviews priorities and validates key outputs. Members participate in their individual capacity.

Scientific coordination

Supports analysis, methodological rigour, documentary management and project development.

Sub-Working Groups & Projects

Operate under PIC leadership. A SWG can group projects around a theme; projects may also stand alone.

Geneva Health Forum

Provides the institutional home. SWG and project lead structures require dual PIC/GHF approval.

The later Partnership Framework clarifies that SWGs and standalone projects sit at the same operational level, and that lead structures require dual approval.

Programme direction

Strategic Workstreams of the PIC

Four potential workstreams share an analytical method and a cross-cutting lens of education, awareness and behaviour change. Groups are activated progressively according to priorities, expertise and resources.

The framework’s three analytical stages lead towards project implementation. Following Sara’s website review, implementation appears as the fourth stage on the homepage.

Contributing to PIC

PIC Partnership Framework

Project contributors are classified according to the nature of their contribution. Funding alone does not confer partner status or governance authority.

Institutional home

Geneva Health Forum

PIC’s institutional home, convening platform and coordination environment.

The supplied framework identifies GHF / University of Geneva as host institution. Scientific coordination supports PIC’s work and reports to GHF Direction.

The Partnership Framework gives GHF a separate role in reviewing the alignment of people and organisations involved in its hosted initiatives, alongside PIC approval.
